title: A Sea of Tears
text:
You will suffer. You have already suffered.

Perhaps you are suffering.

And though you know

why (if you know it),

that knowledge will not be your consolation.


The farewell to your own; chance,

implacable; the unknown of

heaven,

everything that is lost

down deeds and life, down time,


or also up through life, toward what awaits you,

everything shapes the

flavor of your tears,

a flavor without flavor, since it is not shared


by the one who has seen you suffer

—he cannot share it—,

a flavor you do not

understand,

a heap of tears that traces,

I do not know where,

a

sea across which there drift,

and I do not know why,

useless forever,

inconsolable,

who knows since when,

his soul,

your soul

and

mine.

From

"" 1996
editorial_note: The translation keeps Marzal's address to suffering and the strange, unresolved bibliographic fragment at the end.

title: I Will Play with the Houses of Curaçao
text:
I will play with the houses of Curaçao,

I will put the sea on the left

and make more drawbridges.

Whatever the poet says!

We are in Holland and in America

and it is a toy-store island,

with decrees of the Queen

and windows and doors of joy.

With the strings of the lyre

and the handkerchiefs from the journey

we will make sails for the boats

that go nowhere.

The Government House is too small

for a Dutch family.

In the afternoon Claude Monet will come

to eat blue and electric things.

And down that suspicious alley

we will make Rembrandt's Night Watch pass.

...Pass me the port of Curaçao!

Toy-store island,

with decrees of the Queen

and windows and doors of joy.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Pellicer's playful island as a toy-like, painterly Curaçao between Holland and America.

title: Desires
text:
Tropic, why did you give me

hands full of color.

Everything I touch

will fill with sun.

On subtle afternoons in other lands

I will pass with my noises of iridescent glass.

Let me for a single instant

stop being cry and color.

Let me for a single instant

change the climate of my heart,

drink the half-light of a deserted thing,

lean in silence over a distant balcony,

sink into the mantle of fine folds,

scatter myself on the shore of a gentle devotion,

gently caress the straight hair

and write my meditation with a very fine pencil.

Oh, to stop being for a single instant

the sun's aide-de-camp!

Tropic, why did you give me

hands full of color!
editorial_note: The translation preserves Pellicer's wish to step outside tropical color and become briefly quiet and shaded.
